Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Getting started
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Netrun turns Hacking Expansion into a whole network game: your hacks leave a digital trace (Heat), fixers sell services and contracts, awakened AIs live on your servers, and netrunners dive into cyberspace for loot.
## Your first steps
Ticked from your game as you go:
[[checklist]]
Until the colony touches the net, Netrun's threats do not come (newcomer protection).

tips.li: F1 in the terminal opens the Cyberpedia on the current screen.
The book button in the terminal's title is a guide: it highlights the areas of a screen and explains each one.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: The terminal
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: The terminal is a map of nodes around the Core; each node is a part of your network. Click one to read what it holds. Nodes open one by one as you meet them in the game.\n[[terminalmap]]\n> open:Core|Open the Core

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Hacks and cyberdata
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
A hacker colonist (with a cyberlink) can hack devices on the map, or do it from a cyberpod. Each finished hack gives cyberdata and raises Heat. Try how much trace one hack leaves:
[[hackheat]]
## !thing:USH_Cyberdata Cyberdata
The currency of the net: dives, programs, scrubbing the trace with a fixer. Advanced cyberdata is worth three times more.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Newcomer protection
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: Until the colony touches the net (any Heat, a cyberpod or server built, a colonist with a cyberlink, or a dive), the heavy threats wait. Here is how it stands:\n[[newcomer]]\nThe protection can be turned off in the mod settings.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Heat and trace
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Heat is your colony's digital trace, from 0 to 100. Every hack and dive raises it. The higher it is, the more attention the net pays to you: network attacks, mercenary raids, corporate hunts.
[[levels]]
Heat cools by itself: −{heat.decay} a day, −{heat.decayHigh} at Target and above.
> open:Heat|Open the "Heat and trace" screen

tips.li: Scrub the trace while you are below Target: it is cheaper.
A Ghost AI and the Wraith daemon reduce the trace of your hacks and dives.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Levels and their effects
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
[[cards]]
- !heat:Shadow Shadow (0–24): Nobody is looking. No attacks; fixers scrub at their best rate.
- !heat:Noticed Noticed (25–49): Neural noise and data theft can come.
- !heat:Tracked Tracked (50–74): Malware breakdowns and power surges join in; hackers may hijack your turrets while a netrunner is in a pod. Scrubbing gets less effective.
- !heat:Target Target (75–94): Ransomware, Black Book mercenary raids, the corporate hunt for your AI server, ICE hunters in dives. Heat cools twice as slowly; "Quiet run" contracts fail.
- !heat:RedZone Red Zone (95–100): Everything from Target, with the worst scrub rate. The exact list for your current level is on the Heat screen under "Level effects".

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: How to lower Heat
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Four ways down, compared for the Heat you pick (your own settings):
[[lowerheat]]
## !Fixers/Fixer_Corp Through a fixer
Call a fixer in the Club (silver opens a channel for {fixers.channel} hours) and hand over cyberdata. The rate falls as Heat grows: from {heat.scrubBest} Heat per cyberdata in the Shadow to {heat.scrubWorst} in the Red Zone.
> page:NR_Help_Fixers_Scrub|How a scrub works
> open:Heat|Ways to lower on the Heat screen

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Netsick
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Netsick is a netrunner's dependency on cyberspace. It grows with time in a pod, dives ({netsick.dive} per dive) and Black ICE hits, and fades offline.
[[netsick]]
## Stages
- Mild: no effect yet.
- Noticeable (30%+): after a day offline, the mood drops ("reality feels flat").
- Strong (60%+): a little less consciousness, "net craving" breaks every few days.
- Severe (85%+): worse mood and more frequent breaks.
## Treatment
Time offline is the cure, and live leisure doubles it: talks, walks and meditation, games, the telescope, art (screens and drugs do not count). A neurostabilizer (drug lab: 1 neutroamine and 2 cyberdata) takes off 15% at once and holds the withdrawal and the craving off for two days, but taken often it hooks like smokeleaf. A Doc AI eases it; an AI in a AI coprocessor reduces the growth. A dive every 2–3 days keeps Netsick steady; daily dives build a strong dependency.
## Traits
- Natural netrunner (a rare trait): Netsick grows 40% slower, hacks in dives +5%.
- Neurotic: Netsick grows 15% faster (very neurotic 30%).
- Industrious: it fades 15% faster offline (hard worker 30%); lazy 15% slower.
The bottom bar of the terminal shows how many colonists have it.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: AI traits
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: Besides its archetype, each AI may have traits of its own. Every trait helps and hurts; pick one to read both sides:\n[[aitraits]]

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: What a dive leaves behind
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Besides Netsick and burns, a dive can leave a mark on the netrunner. Every one shows in the dive summary.
## Good
- Net flow: a clean exit with no ICE hits. A day of faster learning and research, hacks in dives +5%.
- Digital memory: sometimes a successful dive brings back experience in a random skill.
- Survived the ICE: a success after an ICE hit lifts the mood.
## Bad
- Digital migraine: a long dive (9 turns or more). Pain and less consciousness for half a day.
- Phantom signals: at strong Netsick the runner may see ICE in the real world and wander off.
- Burned link: a failed Black ICE dive after a hit. Hacks in dives −10% for three days.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Netrun and the rest of the game
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
## Hacking Expansion
A hackable target shows in its info how much Heat a hack would leave (less with hacking stealth or from a cyberpod).
## Pawn traits
- Natural netrunner (a rare new trait): Netsick grows 40% slower, hacks in dives +5%.
- Neurotic: Netsick grows faster. Industrious: it fades faster offline; lazy: slower.
## Ideology (DLC)
The "net culture" issue: sacred (a dive is communion, a good mood), wary (a dive is unsettling, high Heat weighs on the mood), abhorrent (a dive is a disgrace, any trace stains the colony).
## Royalty (DLC)
Imperial clients join the fixer pool while you are at peace with the Empire: less silver, royal favor for finished contracts.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Fixers and contracts
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Fixers are your contacts in the net. They scrub your trace, sell goods and give contracts. Calling a fixer costs silver and opens a channel for {fixers.channel} hours.
[[cards]]
- !Fixers/Fixer_ShadowBroker The pool and reputation: five fixers, a slider shows what reputation opens. [[NR_Help_Fixers_Pool|Read]]
- !Fixers/Fixer_Street Specialties and traits: who does what, and how each trait helps and hurts. [[NR_Help_Fixers_Types|Read]]
- !Nodes/Home_Board Contracts: the stages of a job and every kind with real numbers. [[NR_Help_Fixers_Contracts|Read]]
- !Heat/Heat_Reduction Scrubbing the trace: cyberdata for Heat, try the calculator. [[NR_Help_Fixers_Scrub|Read]]
- !Fixers/Fixer_Shop Shop and black market: a fence's price list. [[NR_Help_Fixers_Market|Read]]

tips.li: Hold a fixer you like so they stay through the rotation.
A fixer with 'Rat' may leak your deals: watch their trait.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: The pool and reputation
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: The pool has {fixers.pool} fixers and changes every {fixers.rotation} days. Unpinned fixers leave unless a contract with them is running or you hold them. Pick a fixer and move their reputation: the trait shows from the purple mark, pinning comes at the gold one, and prices and the scrub rate change with it (the same formulas the game uses).\n[[fixerpool]]

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Specialties and traits
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Every fixer has a specialty and a trait. Pick one to read it:
[[cards]]
- !Fixers/Fixer_ShadowBroker Broker: lives on contracts: more offers and better pay for data.
- !Fixers/Fixer_Corp Cleaner: scrubs the trace cheaper than anyone.
- !Fixers/Fixer_Street Fence: runs a shop: goods for silver, rare items for pinned contacts.
- !Fixers/Fixer_Corp Imperial client: comes only while you are at peace with the Empire (Royalty). Pays less silver, but each finished contract adds royal favor to the colonist the Empire knows best.
## Traits (each helps and hurts)
[[cards]]
- Greedy: more goods / everything a quarter dearer.
- Reliable: forgives half a failure, sends no one after you / rewards −10%.
- Rat: everything 20% cheaper / may sell you out (+Heat).
- Paranoid: revenge raids come 25% weaker / no calls at Tracked or higher.
- Gambler: the pay is rolled on completion (half to almost double).
- Loyal: reputation twice as fast, extra discount once pinned / will not work while a rival of his trade is pinned.
- Veteran: scrub 20% better / the call 30% dearer.
- Collector: rare goods always in the shop / fewer ordinary ones.
- Hothead: contracts pay 40% more / 40% shorter, a failure adds Heat.
Cleaners are often veterans, fences often collectors. A trait stays hidden until reputation {fixers.pin} or until the fixer gives themselves away.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Contracts
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: Each fixer offers contracts on the Board. Click a stage to see what happens there, then a kind of contract to see an example with the real numbers.\n[[contractflow]]\n> open:Board|Open the Board

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Scrubbing the trace
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
With an open channel, "Scrub" in the Club (or on the Heat screen) lets you choose how much cyberdata to give. Each cyberdata removes {heat.scrubBest} Heat in the Shadow and only {heat.scrubWorst} in the Red Zone; advanced counts triple. Every unit is priced at the level the Heat stands at when you spend it, so one big scrub costs the same as many small ones. Try it:
[[scrub]]
Reputation and the Cleaner specialty give discounts, a greedy fixer charges more.
!Fixer_Service_Reward A fixer's service found in cyberspace is a free scrub.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Shop and black market
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: Fences sell goods for silver: the price is the item's value with the shop's markup, lower with reputation. Pinned fences add rare items, and in the black market event fixers who trust you sell what is not in their stock, dearer. Try it:\n[[market]]

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: AI and the server room
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
An AI fragment from cyberspace or a hack can be awakened on an AI server. Each AI has an archetype with its own service, food and character, and up to two traits of its own. Archetypes you have met open in the gallery; the rest stay "???". Move the trust slider to see what an AI gives and when it turns against you.
[[cards]]
- !Tabs/Tab_AI AI archetypes: the gallery of the thirteen, with trust. [[NR_Help_AI_Archetypes|Read]]
- !Gizmo_AI_Use Homes, trust and hunger: server, coprocessor or host. [[NR_Help_AI_Basics|Read]]
- !Gizmo_AI_Feed Feeding and requests: hunger over the days. [[NR_Help_AI_Feeding|Read]]
- !thing:NR_AIFragment Fragments and awakening: where they come from. [[NR_Help_AI_Awaken|Read]]
- !Icon_AIRequest AI traits: ten traits, each with a plus and a minus. [[NR_Help_AI_Traits|Read]]
> open:Server|Open the server room

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Homes, trust and hunger
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
An AI can live in three places, and each gives something different. Click a home:
[[aihomes]]
## !Gizmo_AI_Use Trust and services
A service needs {ai.minTrust} trust, costs {ai.serviceTrust} trust and {ai.serviceHunger} hunger, then rests {ai.cooldown} days. Starving or betrayed AIs make trouble and may escape into the net.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Feeding and requests
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Every archetype eats something of its own (see the archetypes). Hunger grows every day; above {ai.starving} the AI starves and loses trust. Play with the days:
[[aihunger]]
## !Icon_AIRequest Requests
Now and then an AI asks for something: a double meal, attention, silence. Do it in time for trust; ignore it and trust drops.
> open:Server|Open the server room

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Fragments and awakening
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: A fragment is a sleeping AI. A colonist carries it to a powered AI server with a free slot and wakes it there; the archetype is revealed at waking.\n[[aiawaken]]\n!Gizmo_AI_Erase An AI can be erased for advanced cyberdata.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: AI archetypes
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: Every awakened AI has one of thirteen archetypes. Archetypes you have met open here; the rest stay "?" until you wake one. Pick an archetype to see its service and food, then move the trust slider: it shows when the service works, when traits show, and when the AI turns against you.\n[[aigallery]]

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Cyberspace
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
The Gateway is the map of foreign systems around your node. A netrunner in a cyberpod dives into a node, walks its steps and brings the loot home. Every step leaves a trace, and after the dive the trace turns into Heat. New nodes come every {dive.refresh} days; hidden ones can be found for {dive.search} cyberdata.
## The Gateway map
Each node shows its type by colour and icon. Click one to see its card: defense, risk, how much trace a step costs there and what it pays.
[[gateway]]
## How a dive goes
Steps are crossed one by one: gates to hack, hidden steps to scan, files to download, ICE that strikes back. At a fork you pick the easy or the hard branch; you cannot step back out of it. Forgot the files? "Back" returns one step and costs the turn.
[[dive]]
## Hack chance
The netrunner's Intellectual helps, the strength of the gate hurts; programs, daemons and the runner's state add or take a little. Try it:
[[hackchance]]
## Trace and Heat
The trace of a dive is multiplied by the node type: corp nodes leave the most. Quiet news and stealth help.
[[trace]]
> page:NR_Help_Gateway_Nodes|Node types in detail
> page:NR_Help_Gateway_Ice|ICE and Black ICE
> page:NR_Help_Gateway_Effects|What a dive leaves behind
> open:Gateway|Open the Gateway

tips.li: Middle mouse button on the Gateway field resets the camera.
A clean exit gives the full haul and a chance of a special find.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Node types
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
[[cards]]
- !Node_Market Market: Easy and quick: some cyberdata.
- !Node_Archive Archive: Files and memory with data.
- !Node_CorpVault Corporate vault: Strong gates, advanced cyberdata, often Black ICE.
- !Node_AbandonedServer Abandoned server: Weak defense, memory units with AI fragments; sometimes a wild AI.
- !Node_DarkExchange Dark exchange: Silver on top of the data. Bigger circles pay more. ★ marks a node a contract wants.
- !Node_CorpCore Corporate core: Every {dive.boss} days a boss node appears for a few days: four gates and strong Black ICE. Cracking it gives a daemon (or a celebrity chip), maybe a core module, and a big haul.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: How a dive goes
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
A dive is a path of steps from the lobby to the exit:
[[dive]]
Each turn you have a few actions:
[[cards]]
- !Action_Move Move to the next step.
- !Action_Scan Scan: reveal hidden steps (caches, honeypots).
- !Action_Hack Hack a gate or ICE.
- !Action_Download Download files or memory.
- !Action_Exit Exit from the I/O port with everything.
Every action raises the dive's trace; after your actions the node takes its turn and Black ICE may strike. You have {dive.turns} turns (more on nodes with forks).
## !Dive_BLACKICE Forks
Medium nodes split once, large ones and the corporate core twice. The hard path pays more (haul ×{dive.hardReward}) but Black ICE guards it and the trace is louder (+{dive.hardTrace}); the easy path is quiet (+{dive.easyTrace}), pays less (×{dive.easyReward}) and hides a passage that adds to the haul. Scan at the fork to see the numbers. The choice is final and costs no action; from the first fork you can still leave for free. Retreating early from the lobby is free; deeper it costs part of the haul. Leaving the pod takes {dive.wake} hours.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: ICE and Black ICE
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
[[ice]]
## !Dive_GATE Code gates
Walls you must hack; strength grows with the node's defense.
## !Dive_ICE ICE
Hacking Expansion's defense: it can trace, lock out or hurt the hacker.
## !Dive_BLACKICE Black ICE
A killer program on a step of the node. It strikes every node turn: nausea, a lockout (the dive ends) or a coma. A Shield absorbs a strike, a Decoy may draw it off, a Killer breaks it.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Programs and daemons
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
[[loadout]]
Programs are loaded before a dive: {dive.slots} slots, {dive.program} cyberdata each.
- !Program_Sword Sword: easier hacks.
- !Program_Shield Shield: absorbs an ICE strike.
- !Program_Decoy Decoy: may draw ICE away.
- !Program_Stealth Stealth: half the trace.
- !Program_Killer Killer: breaks ICE.
## Daemons
Daemons are permanent programs found in cyberspace (often in the corporate core): free and without a slot, but you take only one per dive.
- !Daemon_Reaper Reaper: hacks much easier.
- !Daemon_Aegis Aegis: a Shield charge every dive.
- !Daemon_Wraith Wraith: half the trace.
- !Daemon_Hound Hound: a Killer charge every dive.
- !Daemon_Lens Lens: hidden caches are always visible.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Rewards and the summary
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Files pay back the cost of the dive with a multiplier: more for stronger nodes, most with Black ICE. On a clean exit there is a chance of a special find:
[[cards]]
- !thing:NR_AIFragment AI fragment: a sleeping AI, waiting for your server.
- !Tabs/Tab_Rewards Research: progress on the project you are researching.
- !Fixer_Service_Reward A fixer's service: a free scrub of the trace from a fixer in the pool.
- !Icon_GroupFavor The group's favor: a step toward calling the hacker group.
- !thing:NR_BraindanceChip Celebrity braindance: a recorded memory of someone famous.
- !Reward_DaemonProgram Daemon: a permanent program for every later dive.
- !thing:NR_AICoreModule Core module: one more slot for the AI server.
!Icon_DiveReport After a dive the summary shows the haul, the costs, Heat and Netsick (can be turned off in the settings).

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: The hacker group
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: !Icon_GroupFavor Sometimes a dive's special find is a favor for a hacker group. At {dive.favor} favor, "Call the group" in the Club sends allied fighters (or advanced cyberdata if you have no allies); then the group rests {dive.allies} days.
Netrun.HelpPageDef.lockHint: Opens when you first earn the group's favor.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Braindance
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Braindance lets colonists live through someone else's memories.
[[cards]]
- !Gizmo_BD_Record Goggles and recording: how a strong moment becomes a raw recording. [[NR_Help_BD_Record|Read]]
- !thing:NR_BraindanceChip Editing and chips: the mood decides the chip; try it. [[NR_Help_BD_Chips|Read]]
- !thing:NR_BlackBraindanceChip Black braindance: a stronger rush and a stronger hook. [[NR_Help_BD_Black|Read]]
- !Reward_UniqueBraindance Unique recordings: eight named memories with effects of their own. [[NR_Help_BD_Unique|Read]]
> open:Studio|Open the Studio

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Goggles and recording
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Braindance goggles record their wearer's strongest moments by themselves. The result is a raw recording: a memory waiting to be edited.
[[cards]]
- !thing:NR_BraindanceGoggles Goggles: craft them at a fabrication bench (Crafting 5) and put them on a colonist. Only the goggles record; a cyberlink can watch chips but does not record.
- !Gizmo_BD_Record What gets recorded: a strong feeling (a big mood swing, joy or grief) or a kill. The goggles capture it on their own.
- !thing:NR_BraindanceRaw The raw recording: it keeps the moment's mood (bright, dark or combat) and its strength, and lies next to the colonist. It is not a chip yet and cannot be watched.
- !Icon_Lock One a day: at most one recording a day per colonist, so a bad day does not flood the storage.
- !Nodes/Home_Studio Where to see them: the Studio's "Raw recordings" tab lists every raw recording on the map with its author, mood and quality.
> page:NR_Help_BD_Chips|Editing and chips
> open:Studio|Open the Studio

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Editing and chips
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Editing turns a raw recording into a chip that anyone with goggles or a cyberlink can watch. Switch the mood and the strength of the moment: the chip, its quality and its effect change.
[[braindance]]
## !Gizmo_BD_Watch Watching
A colonist plays a chip with goggles or a cyberlink, like a drug: recreation and a mood, and regular use builds tolerance. Put chips in the drug policy to decide who may watch them and how often.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Black braindance and addiction
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body: [[braindance:Dark]]\nBlack chips hold real pain, fear and death. The rush is far stronger than any ordinary recording, and so is the risk of addiction: without regular braindances an addict gets withdrawal.
Netrun.HelpPageDef.lockHint: Opens when you get a black chip.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Unique recordings
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Rare named recordings with an effect of their own: a mood that lasts days, a skill edge, a market know-how, a glimpse of the future. There are eight, and they are rare; the same one can turn up again.
## Where to find them
[[cards]]
- !Node_CorpCore The corporate core, sometimes instead of a daemon.
- !Reward_Valuables A dive's special find.
- !Event_BlackMarket The black market, now and then, for a high price.
- !Fixers/Handshake A fixer's bonus for a finished contract.
## Watching
Like any chip: braindance goggles or a cyberlink. A recording lasts 1 to 3 views, then burns out. Ordinary ones do not hook; black ones hook faster than a black chip. The Studio's library shows what you have found and keeps "???" for the rest.
> open:Studio|Open the Studio

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Events
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Netrun brings four groups of events. The frequency of each group can be changed in the mod settings; everything that touches your trace is logged in the Archive.
[[cards]]
- !Event_Cyberspace_Ransomware Network attacks: what the net throws at you as Heat grows. [[NR_Help_Events_Attacks|Read]]
- !Event_MapEvents Map events: couriers, hunts, the black market, the distress signal. [[NR_Help_Events_Map|Read]]
- !Tabs/Tab_Events_Cyberspace Cyberspace events: hunters, rivals, storms and the news. [[NR_Help_Events_Cyber|Read]]
- !Tabs/Tab_Events_AI AI events: what your AIs do on their own. [[NR_Help_Events_AI|Read]]
> open:Archive|Open the Archive

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Network attacks
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Come from the storyteller as Heat grows.
[[cards]]
- Neural noise (Noticed+): a hacker's mind is flooded with garbage signal. Lower Heat or wait it out.
- !Event_Cyberspace_DataTheft Data theft (Noticed+): cyberdata disappears from your storage.
- !Event_Cyberspace_MalwareBreakdown Malware breakdown (Tracked+): machines break down; keep components ready.
- !Event_Cyberspace_PowerSurge Power surge (Tracked+): batteries drain, devices spark.
- !Event_Cyberspace_Ransomware Ransomware (Target+): pay silver or lose more.
- !Faction_Mercenaries Mercenary raids (Target+, or as revenge): the Black Book comes armed.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Map events
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
- !Event_DataCourier Data courier: a fixer's courier with cyberdata stays a day; mercenaries come for the data. Keep them alive for silver and reputation, or take the data: if the courier dies, the cyberdata is yours, but the job fails.
[[cards]]
- !Event_CorpHunt Corporate hunt (Target+, with an AI server): a corporate team comes for your server.
- !Event_BlackMarket Black market: rare goods at trusted fixers for a few days.
- !Event_DistressSignal Distress signal: a quest in the Quests tab. An abandoned server sits in a sealed compound on the world map, guarded by turrets (and hunter drones with Odyssey); reach it and connect for an AI fragment (or ICE backlash).
- !Event_MapHack Turret hijack (Tracked+, netrunner in a pod): turrets switch off; dive into the counter-hack node to take them back.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Cyberspace events
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
- !Event_HunterICE ICE hunter (Target+): strikes every node turn; hack it or leave before it follows you home.
[[cards]]
- !Event_Rival Rival netrunner: takes the files after a few turns; be faster.
- !Event_Honeypot Too good to be true: now and then a node looks richer than it should. Trust your scans more than your greed.
- !Event_DataStorm Data storm: harder gates, bigger haul for a day or two.
- !Event_WildAI Wild AI: in an abandoned server; tame it, erase it or sell it.
- !Node_Counterhack Counter-hack: the node to free your hijacked turrets.
## News that changes the net
Every few days the news line reports something with a real effect: a node hardens its ICE or has its codes leaked, data floods the market (more cyberdata from dives), the net goes quiet (less trace). When the corporate core falls, corp nodes go on lockdown for a week. A runaway AI hides in an abandoned node: dive there to find it.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: AI events
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
Awakened AIs are not tools: they want things and act on their own. Now and then one of them does something, and what it does depends on who it is and how it feels.
[[cards]]
- !Icon_AIRequest What drives them: Trust: a trusting AI brings gifts, favors and help; a resentful one plays tricks and makes trouble. Hunger: a hungry AI gets restless, and its events turn darker. Home: an AI behaves differently on the server, in a cyberpod's coprocessor and inside a host.
- !Gizmo_AI_Use Letters and choices: Most events come as a letter. Some simply happen; others offer up to three answers. Leaving a letter unanswered is an answer too.
- Archetypes: Any AI can have the general events, and every archetype has several of its own that fit its character. A new archetype means new surprises.
- What can change: Trust and hunger, Heat, your stores, your colonists' mood, skills and health, the work of your machines and sometimes your dealings with fixers. The letter always says what is at stake.

Netrun.HelpPageDef.label: Settings and bug reports
Netrun.HelpPageDef.body:
## Bug reports
Press the button and paste what it copies into your bug report: versions, DLC, mods, changed settings and the last Netrun errors. No personal data.
[[diagnostics]]
Options → Mod settings → Hacking Expansion: Netrun.
- !Dive_Heat Heat difficulty (Easy, Normal, Hard) and fine sliders.
- !Tabs/Tab_Events_Blue Frequency of each event group, from off to x2.
- !Icon_Lock Newcomer protection, the dive summary, pause on open, animations.
Found a bug? "Copy info for a bug report" puts versions and your mod list into the clipboard: paste it into the bug report on GitHub with your Player.log.
